title: From Milk Tea to a Budget: A Young Person's First Guide to Money
title_zh: 从奶茶到预算：年轻人的第一堂理财课
intro_zh: 本文约 516 词，围绕年轻人理财入门展开，从预算、记账、储蓄、应急金、债务到投资层层推进，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: The first paycheck feels like a small fortune. For many young people in China, the moment money appears in their bank account is exciting — and a little confusing. Rent, phone bills, meals with friends, new clothes: the list grows quietly. By the middle of the month, the account may look almost empty, and no one is quite sure where the money went.
paragraphs.zh: 第一笔工资感觉像一笔小财富。对中国许多年轻人来说，钱出现在银行账户里的那一刻既令人兴奋，又让人有点困惑。房租、话费、和朋友聚餐、新衣服：清单在悄悄变长。到了月中，账户可能看起来几乎空了，而没有人真正清楚钱花到哪里去了。

paragraphs.en: This is where a budget helps. A budget is simply a plan for your money. It does not mean saying no to every coffee or movie. Instead, it means deciding in advance how much goes to each part of life: food, transport, rent, fun, and savings. A common and friendly rule is 50-30-20: half for needs, thirty percent for wants, and twenty percent for the future. The exact numbers matter less than the habit of looking.
paragraphs.zh: 这时候预算就有用了。预算不过是你对钱的一个计划。它并不意味着对每一杯咖啡、每一场电影都说“不”。相反，它意味着提前决定每个生活部分花多少钱：吃饭、交通、房租、娱乐和储蓄。一个常见而友好的规则是 50-30-20：一半用于必需，百分之三十用于想要，百分之二十用于未来。具体数字并没有养成查看的习惯那么重要。

paragraphs.en: Many people are surprised when they finally write down their expenses. Small daily choices — a milk tea here, a taxi there — can add up to hundreds of yuan a month. A simple notebook or a free phone app is enough. After two or three weeks, patterns appear: maybe delivery food is the quiet thief, or maybe weekend shopping is. Seeing the truth is the first step to changing it.
paragraphs.zh: 很多人在最终把自己的开支记下来时都会感到惊讶。每天的小选择——这里一杯奶茶，那里一次打车——一个月加起来可能达到几百元。一个简单的笔记本或一个免费的手机应用就足够了。两三周之后，规律就会显现：也许外卖是那个安静的小偷，也许周末购物才是。看到真相，是改变它的第一步。

paragraphs.en: Next comes savings. The trick is to save first, not last. When the paycheck arrives, move a small amount — even fifty or one hundred yuan — into a separate account before you spend anything. This is called paying yourself first. The amount can grow slowly. What matters is that the money is not sitting in the same account as your daily spending, where it is too easy to use.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来是储蓄。诀窍是先存钱，而不是最后才存。工资一到账，在你花任何钱之前，先把一小笔钱——哪怕五十或一百元——转到一个单独的账户里。这就叫先付给自己。金额可以慢慢增加。重要的是，这笔钱不要和你的日常开销放在同一个账户里，因为那样太容易花掉了。

paragraphs.en: Experts also suggest building an emergency fund. This is money kept for unexpected events: a broken laptop, a medical bill, or a sudden trip home. For a student or a young worker, even one month of basic costs is a good start; three to six months is a safer goal. This fund protects you from borrowing money when life surprises you.
paragraphs.zh: 专家还建议建立一笔应急基金。这是为意外事件保留的钱：笔记本电脑坏了、一笔医疗账单，或者一次突然回家。对学生或年轻上班族来说，哪怕只是一个月的日常基本开销也是不错的开始；三到六个月是更稳妥的目标。当生活给你意外时，这笔钱能让你不必去借钱。

paragraphs.en: Debt deserves careful attention. Used well, a credit card is convenient and can build a good record. Used carelessly, it becomes a trap, because unpaid balances grow with interest. A simple rule: pay the full amount every month, and never borrow for things that disappear quickly, like meals or clothes.
paragraphs.zh: 债务值得仔细对待。用得好，信用卡很方便，还能帮你建立良好的记录。用得粗心，它就会变成一个陷阱，因为未还清的余额会随着利息增长。一个简单的原则：每月全额还款，绝不要为那些很快就消失的东西借钱，比如吃饭或衣服。

paragraphs.en: Once savings and a small emergency fund are in place, some young people begin to invest. Investing means putting money into something — such as a fund or a company — hoping it will grow over time. It carries risk, so it should come after the basics are covered. Starting early, even with a small amount, gives time a chance to work. But no one should invest money they may need next month.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦储蓄和一小笔应急基金都到位了，一些年轻人就开始投资。投资意味着把钱投入到某样东西里——比如基金或一家公司——希望它随着时间增长。它带有风险，所以应当在基础打好之后再做。早点开始，即使金额很小，也能让时间发挥作用。但没有人应该把下个月可能需要的钱拿去投资。

paragraphs.en: None of this requires a finance degree. It requires a few simple habits: know what comes in, decide what goes out, and keep something for later. The goal is not to become rich overnight. It is to feel calm and in control — and that feeling, for a young person just starting out, may be the most valuable thing of all.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都不需要金融学位。它需要的只是几个简单的习惯：知道进来多少，决定出去多少，并为以后留一点。目标不是一夜暴富，而是感到平静、感到自己在掌控之中——对一个刚刚起步的年轻人来说，这种感觉也许才是最宝贵的东西。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain how young people can manage money step by step.
To warn readers against using credit cards.
To compare banks and phone apps.
To prove that investing is the fastest way to get rich.
questions.explain: 全文围绕年轻人如何一步步管理钱财展开，依次讲到预算、记账、储蓄、应急金、债务和投资，故选 A。B 只涉及第六段一个细节，C、D 与原文不符（文中说投资带有风险，目标不是一夜暴富）。

questions.q: According to the passage, what does the 50-30-20 rule suggest?
options: People should spend half of their income on fun.
People should save at least fifty percent of their income.
Half of the income goes to needs, thirty percent to wants, and twenty percent to the future.
The exact numbers matter more than the habit of looking.
questions.explain: 第二段明确说明 50-30-20 规则：一半用于必需，百分之三十用于想要，百分之二十用于未来，故选 C。A、B 曲解了比例；D 与原文相反，原文说具体数字没有那么重要。

questions.q: What can be inferred about keeping savings in the same account as daily spending?
options: It is the best way to pay yourself first.
It makes the money easy to spend without noticing.
It helps young people build a good credit record.
It protects the money from unexpected events.
questions.explain: 第四段说储蓄要和日常开销分开，因为放在同一个账户里“太容易花掉”，可推断这样会在不知不觉中把钱花掉，故选 B。A 与原文做法相反；C、D 分别属于信用卡和应急基金的内容。

questions.q: What does the word 'trap' in paragraph 6 most probably mean?
options: A useful tool for daily shopping
A monthly payment to the bank
A difficult situation that is hard to escape
questions.explain: 第六段说信用卡若粗心使用就会成为 trap，原因是未还清的余额会随利息不断增长，可见它指一种难以摆脱的困境，故选 D。A 与语义相反，B、C 均非 trap 的意思。
